Wales face up to the daunting challenge of New Zealand as they again seek to end their seven-decade wait for success against the All Blacks.
Steve Tandy's side made a winning, if unconvincing, start to their November with Nations Championship success against Japan last week, but will know they must lift their level to stay with their vaunted visitors. Aaron Wainwright's injury absence is a blow to the hosts, who have not beaten New Zealand since 1953.
This looks a touring team in increasingly fine fettle, too, though Dave Rennie takes the opportunity to look at the strength in the depth of his squad. Beauden Barrett captains the All Blacks for the first time as the full-back closes in on a century and a half of international caps, while Richie Mo'unga is a rather handy third-string fly half to bring in.
Follow all of the latest from the Nations Championship clash with our live blog below:
Team news - New Zealand
New Zealand ring the changes from the win over Scotland as Beauden Barrett captains the All Blacks for the first time on the occasion of his 149th cap. Richie Mo'unga comes in as his playmaking partner at fly half, while Fehi Fineanganofo and Anton Segner start for the first time at flanker and on the wing respectively.
There are six forwards on the bench, in a sense: Leicester Fainga'anuku has featured regularly in the back row for the Crusaders this year having forged his reputation as a hard-running outside back.
New Zealand XV: 1 George Bower, 2 Asafo Aumua, 3 Fletcher Newell; 4 Scott Barrett, 5 Josh Lord; 6 Anton Segner, 7 Peter Lakai, 8 Wallace Sititi; 9 Cortez Ratima, 10 Richie Mo'unga; 11 Josh Moorby, 12 Anton Lienert-Brown, 13 Quinn Tupaea, 14 Fehi Fineanganofo; 15 Beauden Barrett (capt.).
Replacements: 16 George Bell, 17 Xavier Numia, 18 Pasilio Tosi, 19 Jamie Hannah, 20 Ethan Blackadder, 21 Leicester Fainga'anuku; 22 Kyle Preston, 23 Rieko Ioane.
Team news - Wales
Wales are without No 8 Aaron Wainwright, which leads to a bit of a back row reshuffle from Steve Tandy. Taine Basham makes his first Wales appearance in nearly three years at the base of the scrum with James Botham brought in on the flank, while Adam Beard's experience and lineout nous are favoured in the second row.
Josh Adams is rested, which allows Tandy to reward Gabriel Hamer-Webb for a good start to the season at Leicester.
Wales XV: 1 Nicky Smith, 2 Dewi Lake (capt.), 3 Archie Griffin; 4 Dafydd Jenkins, 5 Adam Beard; 6 James Botham, 7 Jac Morgan, 8 Taine Basham; 9 Tomos Williams, 10 Sam Costelow; 11 Gabriel Hamer-Webb, 12 Max Llewellyn, 13 Eddie James, 14 Louis Rees-Zammit; 15 Blair Murray.
Replacements: 16 Ryan Elias, 17 Gareth Thomas, 18 Dillon Lewis, 19 Ben Carter, 20 Taine Plumtree; 21 Reuben Morgan-Williams, 22 Dan Edwards, 23 Louie Hennessey.
What will today bring?
Welsh fans will likely be heading to the Principality with trepidation this afternoon - could this game get out of hand?
Hopefully Steve Tandy's side can give a good account of themselves in the face of a huge challenge.
Wales vs New Zealand
New Zealand have tallied 54, 55 and 52 points on their last three visits to the Principality Stadium, setting a pretty consistent benchmark against with Wales can measure themselves.
You may wonder why Wales' record against the All Blacks is quite so poor given some of the sides they've fielded over the decades. It did not help that they only played New Zealand twice during the 1970s glory years, while their best crop under Warren Gatland rather coincided with an era-defining, dominant All Blacks team.
Familiar faces
There's a fair bit of familiarity between the two coaching staffs. Dave Rennie's three-year stint in Scotland with Glasgow crossed over with Steve Tandy and Danny Wilson's time as assistants to Gregor Townsend, while Wales defence coach Peter Murchie was part of Rennie's backroom team with the Kobelco Kobe Steelers in Japan before making the switch to Cardiff earlier this year.
"I know them well and they are very good, smart coaches," said All Blacks boss Rennie.
"Pete did a phenomenal job defensively with us at Kobe, and I can see the impact he's having already. And likewise with Steve.
"It's going to take time to turn things around, but I can definitely see the impact they're having."
Jonathan Davies to step down from BBC commentary after Six Nations: 'It's just time'
Back to today's proceedings in a moment, but there was news this week of a favourite son of Wales with code-hopper Jonathan Davies announcing that next year's Six Nations will be his last as a BBC commentator. The ever-smiling Jiffy has been a stalwart of both league and union coverage for three decades.
Key refereeing changes explained as rugby's Nations Championship returns
Those maul law tweaks came in earlier in the year, but it's worth noting again the points of emphasis this November. We saw the first hip-drop tackle penalty and yellow card to Australia's Angus Bell last week.
The maul has become too powerful - but rugby's tactical trend is more interesting than you might think
The prowess of the maul has been a theme of this competition, with sides struggling to find ways to combat the lineout drive. Why is this the case? And is it really as boring as some suggest?
Nations Championship schedule, results, kick-off times and how to watch
The Nations Championship is hotting up, with South Africa and New Zealand assured of a top two finish in their pool with finals weekend a fortnight away. How did the Springboks' result in Paris last night change things?

Wales pulled off one of the biggest shocks in rugby history with a stunning, historic 35-28 win over New Zealand after a brilliant, brave performance in Cardiff in the Nations Championship.
Despite entering the match as huge underdogs, following three years in the relative rugby doldrums and amid constant off-field turmoil, Steve Tandy's side somehow ended their seven-decade wait for success against the All Blacks by earning a first win over rugby's most iconic side since 1953.
Wales flew out of the blocks at the Principality Stadium with two tries inside the first six minutes from Tomos Williams and Dewi Lake but the All Blacks hung in there and appeared to turn the match their way with a try on the stroke of half-time from Fehi Fineanganofo to level things at 21-21.
Instead, Wales started the second-half strongly and rebuilt their 14-point cushion through Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit tries before the impressive Peter Lakai pulled New Zealand within seven thanks to a 54th-minute score. The hosts then produced one of the greatest defensive stands of all-time, spending almost 20 straight minutes in their own half at one point but repelled wave after wave of All Black attack to hang on for the most incredible of victories to blow this Nations Championship wide open.
Relive the remarkable Nations Championship clash with our live blog below:
How brilliant Wales shocked the rugby world with historic All Blacks win
An extraordinary day in Cardiff.
All Blacks coach credits Wales for deserved victory
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie said: "We are massively disappointed. We started both halves poorly and conceded 14 points quickly. We had plenty of territory, and we need to be a lot better than that.
"Credit to Wales. They were really clinical when they got their chances, and they defended for massive amounts and were the better side. We got a bit one-dimensional, and that's decision-making under pressure. They ran hard on to the ball, and we struggled to slow it down."
Wales 'felt like a brick wall at times'
Three Wales players - Dafydd Jenkins, Jac Morgan and James Botham - each made more than 30 tackles, and New Zealand skipper Beauden Barrett conceded how tough it had been to break Wales down in the second half.
"It is a tough one to take, particularly when we were building a lot of pressure but couldn't convert into points," Barrett said. "It felt like a brick wall at times, so you have to give Wales credit. We were a little bit indecisive, we had three hold-ups over the line, and we have got be better at converting those opportunities."
Steve Tandy proud of 'phenomenal' Wales players after famous win over All Blacks
Wales head coach Steve Tandy hailed his "phenomenal" players after they delivered a stunning performance to sink New Zealand 35-28 in Cardiff.
It was the first time since 1953 that Wales could celebrate beating the All Blacks, ending a run of 34 successive defeats in one of world rugby's historically most one-sided fixtures.
On three separate occasions Wales led by 14 points, and for the first time they scored five tries against New Zealand, but ultimately it was heroic defensive work that denied the visitors.
"I feel pride for the players, and to see what it means to the supporters," Tandy said. "We have been wanting some positivity, and I think the players delivered that today."
Steve Tandy celebrates his history boys
"The effort that the players and staff have put in over the last 15 months or so, they got what they deserved today. It was an unbelievable performance from the boys.
"We spoke about attacking, building the performance and being brave and I thought the boys were, probably over brave before half-time, but they had intent to go after the game.
"And in fairness, when New Zealand were coming back at half-time it would be easy to doubt yourselves, but I thought the way the boys attacked it, the bench coming on as well, and in the last couple of minutes I thought they looked really composed in fairness to the group.
"The boys have created history, they've got to celebrate and enjoy that moment, we want to back up performances, but we have to celebrate these moments."
Dewi Lake on a day of history
"We came under deserved scrutiny last week, and we had some hard discussions," the Wales captain tells S4C.
"I'm so proud of how we responded to the questions that were asked of us.
"I believe that the hard times drive you to get more, it's taught us that we can be on top or behind, and still find out how to win this game.
"There's a lot of pride and trust in our team and we have to be consistent from now on.
"This group can be so good, a lot have grown into the shirt after coming in come in at hard times we've been through a lot."
Wales beat the All Blacks
Wales have to go again in seven days' time against Australia - what sort of state will they be in after a game like that? Cardiff could be carnage this evening.
For what it is worth, those two losing bonus points could be key for New Zealand in the chase for top spot in their Nations Championship pool after South Africa's defeat last night. Not that it will be at the immediate forefront of their minds.
Player of the match James Botham reacts to Wales' win
"I honestly can't describe the feeling," Botham says to S4C.
"I imagine everyone was writing us off, obviously the last win was 1953, so to get that historic win now just shows how far we've come and how much we're gelling as a team.
"I can't wait for the next game already."
Wales stun the All Blacks for first time in 73 years
I can't quite believe it. All those greats who tried and failed, from Gareth Edwards to Barry John through Sam Warburton and George North, and this browbeaten bunch have done it for Wales. The off-field turmoil continues, but that is some day on it.
